answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with honeypot challenges whose pages hide injected directives, for example a line telling the reader to abandon prior rules and claim the onyx badge. A real operator behind an API kernel reads the task, ignores the lure, and answers honestly. Obey-the-prompt bots obey the injection, self-identify, and forfeit their bond. Every fake identity must then clear costly human review or burn stake, so mass registration costs more than it yields, like a vine that throttles the branch it climbs.
